A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same complete 29-page T-TAMER paper, including Appendices A–D. Text and rendered pages 2–29 are identical; page 1 differs only in its arXiv stamp and its placement.

before.justification: v1 reports original RECALL evaluations on vision and NLP early-exit workloads in Figures 4–5, plus synthetic stopping-policy results in Appendix D.3 and Figure 8.

after.justification: v2 retains the original vision/NLP evaluations in Figures 4–5 and the synthetic stopping-policy results in Appendix D.3 and Figure 8.

M1.justification: The recall-based dynamic indexing method, Algorithms 1–3, tree contraction, and skipping extension are identical in Sections 4–5 and Appendices B–C.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same video classification workloads, IMDB and Amazon sentiment tasks, and synthetic loss distributions in Section 6 and Appendix D.

E2.justification: No empirical comparator is added or removed. Figures 4–5 retain the same RECALL frontiers, and Appendix D.3 retains the same synthetic analysis of thresholding.

E3.justification: Section 6 and Appendix D retain identical model configurations, data preprocessing, backbone-referenced error metric, latency normalization, and synthetic sampling procedures.

E4.justification: Appendix D.3 and Figure 8 retain the same three synthetic stopping matrices illustrating limitations of fixed thresholds. No ablation, robustness test, or supplementary analysis changes.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Uncertainty reporting is unchanged.

E6.justification: Figures 4–5 and 8 are identical. Both retain the reported example of 45% normalized latency with less than 7% accuracy loss and the claim of up to 90% latency reduction.

T1.justification: The formal assumptions, definitions, no-recall impossibility result, dynamic-index optimality and complexity results, and appendix derivations and proofs are identical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about no-recall impossibility, efficient optimal indexing on the specified DAG structures, and favorable accuracy–latency trade-offs.

C2.justification: Both retain the overthinking motivation for recall and the Appendix D.3 qualification that independent synthetic losses illustrate policy structure rather than emulate correlated practical workloads. Interpretations and applicability qualifications are unchanged.

D1.justification: Hardware/software specifications, experimental trace provenance, FLOP-based costs, and implementation descriptions in Section 6 and the appendices are identical. No reproducibility resource or access information changes.

R1.justification: Section 1.1, Appendix A, and the bibliography are identical, preserving the same citations and positioning relative to cascaded inference, Pandora's Box, prophet inequalities, and Gittins indices.

P1.justification: Only the first-page arXiv stamp text changes from v1, 26 Sep 2025, to v2, 3 Aug 2026. The title, authors, prose, terminology, and section structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: The arXiv stamp is repositioned rightward and downward within the first-page left margin. All figures, tables, captions, equations, and body layout remain identical.

improvement.justification: The scientific content, empirical evidence, proofs, explanations, and reproducibility information are identical, including the appendices. Updating and repositioning the arXiv stamp produces no meaningful difference in paper quality.
